subject: FinServ RFP - commercial term sheet and burst credit construct
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finservcorp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finservcorp.com>
Date: 2027-07-12T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: FinServ RFP - commercial clarifications

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier. Procurement asked me to put a short list of commercial clarifications in writing so we can include answers in the RFP appendix (RFP ID: FIN-RFP-2027-06). Please see the items below and attach numbered answers where possible. We have a hard cutover date for procurement review on 2027-07-21, so a consolidated term sheet by COB 2027-07-14 would be ideal.

Key commercial questions:
1) Token pricing: provide per-1k-token list prices for text generation (standard prompt+completion) and for embeddings. Clearly specify units (input vs output) if different.
2) Commit tiers: example bands (0-500M, 500M-2B, 2B+) — what committed rates and step discounts do you propose? Are commits annual or monthly? Can commits be split across business units?
3) Overage mechanics: if actual consumption exceeds commit in a billing period, what is the overage rate? Do you offer smoothing (multi-month true-up) or rolling carryforward credits?
4) Burst protection: for unpredictable spikes, do you provide temporary burst capacity or credits? If so, how is it priced and how fast can it be provisioned?
5) Pilot pricing: we typically run a 30–60 day pilot. What pilot discounts or crediting do you offer and how do you transition pilot usage into a committed plan?
6) Reserved capacity & SLA credits: for Dedicated or Private options, what are minimum reservation requirements and SLA remedies/credits?
7) Invoice & reconciliation: outline how overage invoices are calculated and any reconciliation cadence (monthly true-up, quarterly settlement).

Attached: FinServ_RFP_Questions.pdf (high-level procurement questionnaire).

Short answers are fine; we may follow up with a pricing workbook request.

Best,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Sourcing Manager, FinServ Corp
procurement@finservcorp.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finservcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-12T13:04:00-07:00
Subject: RE: FinServ RFP - commercial clarifications

Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. Below are our proposed commercial responses at a high level; I attached a short term sheet (Redwood_Commercial_Term_Sheet_v1.2.pdf) and a pricing workbook (commit-pricing-model.xlsx) with worked examples. Happy to run through the numbers on a call.

1) Token pricing (list / hosted API):
  - Text generation (prompt + completion, billed per 1K tokens): $0.009 / 1K tokens (standard)
  - Embeddings (per 1K tokens): $0.020 / 1K tokens
  - Notes: list price applies to Hosted. Dedicated/Private deployments are eligible for separate negotiated rates (see commit tiers).

2) Commit tiers (recommended structure, annual commitment default):
  - Band A: 0 — 500M tokens/mo equivalent => $0.008 / 1K (11% off list)
  - Band B: 500M — 2B tokens/mo => $0.0065 / 1K (28% off list)
  - Band C: 2B+ tokens/mo => $0.0048 / 1K (47% off list)
  - Commits can be annual or 12-month monthly locked schedule. Commit-splitting across BU within a single contract is supported (pooling) with per-BU reporting.

3) Overage mechanics:
  - Default: monthly true-up billing at a 20% premium to the committed band rate for the overage portion (i.e., overage rate = committed band rate * 1.20).
  - Smoothing option: we offer a 3-month smoothing window as an add-on where overages are averaged across a rolling 3-month period; extreme single-month spikes are absorbed up to a capped cushion.
  - Carryforward credits: unused committed units can be carried forward up to 25% of monthly commit, for up to 3 months, for annual commit customers.

4) Burst protection:
  - For Hosted customers: we provide Best-Effort burst capacity (subject to available pool) and temporary burst credits priced at 1.35x the committed rate per token.
  - For Dedicated: optional burst reserve (pre-provisioned GPU buffer) can be purchased as a monthly SKU; details in the workbook. Provisioning lead-time ~48–72 hours for reserved bursts, immediate for billed best-effort bursts.

5) Pilot pricing & transition:
  - Pilot credit: standard 60% usage credit for pilots up to 90 days (applies to first 100M tokens).
  - Conversion: pilot usage applied as a one-time credit against the first month(s) of committed usage when you convert to an annual commit.

6) Reserved capacity & SLA credits (Dedicated/Private):
  - Minimum: Dedicated pools typically require a 3-month ramp and a minimum reservation equivalent to 500M tokens/mo or dedicated node equivalent (negotiable).
  - SLA: 99.9% uptime target for Dedicated with service credits tiered (4 hours downtime => 5% monthly credit, >24 hours => 15% credit). Full SLA matrix in term sheet.

7) Invoice & reconciliation:
  - Billing cadence: monthly invoices with a monthly true-up. Annual financial true-up can be requested for enterprise customers.
  - Discrepancies: standard 30-day dispute window; we provide token-level usage reports (CSV) and auditing hooks.

Next steps: we will drop the attached term sheet and pricing workbook into the shared drive link (see Hub reference). If FinServ prefers, we can produce a consolidated single-page commercial summary for procurement and a DocuSign envelope to accelerate signature.

Attachments: Redwood_Commercial_Term_Sheet_v1.2.pdf, commit-pricing-model.xlsx

Thanks — happy to discuss details with Procurement or the technical leads.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0133

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-13T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: FinServ RFP - commercial clarifications (internal)

Internal notes — quick suggestions before we send the consolidated PDF to Elena/Procurement: 

On Tue, Jul 12, 2027 at 1:04 PM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> 3) Overage mechanics:
>   - Default: monthly true-up billing at a 20% premium to the committed band rate for the overage portion...

Proposed edits:
  - Cap the overage premium at 1.2x but introduce an upper cap (no more than $0.0095 / 1K) to avoid sticker-shock for gigantic spikes — keeps procurement conversations civil.
  - For smoothing, prefer a 3-month rolling window (you already proposed) but change carryforward unused commit to 33% (instead of 25%) for enterprise-class annuals — makes the offer stickier and helps close.
  - Add an explicit PS migration fee line (one-time) for Dedicated onboarding ($15k typical) and a 60-day ramp SLA with pro-rated credits if we miss ramp milestones.

If agreed, I'll update the term sheet numbers and regenerate the single-page commercial summary. Also recommend we mark the pilot credit as: 60% credit up to 100M tokens and then 30% credit on the next 100M for larger pilots.

-Marissa
VP Commercial Strategy, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finservcorp.com>

Marcus / Marissa / Karthik —

Thanks for the thoughtful responses and the attachments. Procurement reviewed the high-level term sheet and a few comments:
  - The overage cap suggestion (limit to $0.0095 / 1K) sounds acceptable; please reflect that as a maximum overage floor in the consolidated PDF.
  - Pilot structure looks fine; we will aim for a 60-day pilot scoped at ~100M tokens.
  - Procurement requests a single consolidated PDF (term sheet + worked examples) and a DocuSign-ready contract by COB 2027-07-16 so we can route for internal signatures.

Can you send the consolidated PDF and a DocuSign link? Also include a short note on invoicing terms (net 45) and the contact for Redwood billing.

We'll plan to present the commercial summary to the FinServ steering committee on 2027-07-21. If everything lands cleanly, procurement wants to be ready to issue an LOI the week after.

Best,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Sourcing Manager, FinServ Corp
